title: Fenris Utilities - SCADA onramp & offline inference ramble
content:
Context:
- Fenris Utilities (grid ops) exploring LLM assistant to triage SCADA alerts and suggest next-step remediation to field techs. They insist on air-gapped/offline capability for certain substations and want a staged hybrid POC: cloud-hosted analysis + edge inference in intermittent-connectivity sites.

Call notes (11/03/2025):
- Attendees: Ravi (RW), Elena (RW), Marcus (Fenris infra lead), Priya (Fenris grid ops), Tom (Fenris security).
- Primary ask: quick triage assistant that summarizes alarm chains, recommends priority and likely root cause, suggests checklist items for on-site tech.
- Constraints called out: no PHI/PII but sensitive grid telemetry; per-site data retention rules; some substations must run inference with no outbound traffic for >72h.
- Latency tolerance: interactive for ops dashboard (~300-500ms target for short summaries), but field-device/offline can be batched (1–2s acceptable).
- Typical message sizes: 250–1,200 tokens (compact telemetry + recent logs + event metadata).
- Volume: 700–1,000 inference events/day across 120 sites (peak bursts ~50 concurrent).

Technical considerations / gotchas:
- SCADA logs are time-series + terse tag keys; prompts need canonicalization (map tag ids to human phrases).
- KV cache helps when multiple events reference same asset descriptor (saves tokens).
- On-prem substations: limited GPU (NVIDIA T4 equivalent), intermittent NAT. Need small quantized model (~7B q4) or a small LLM running on CPU with low quality fallback.
- Model choice: start hosted with gpt-like 13B variant for dev POC to reduce hallucination, then propose 7B quantized for edge. Evaluate Redwood's verified models for latency/quality tradeoffs.
- Security: Tom insisted HSM for keys in private sites; attestation for container images; signed prompt/response logging for audits.
- Data residency: EU rules for two sites; ensure routing policy pins those to EU region.

Routing/fallback design sketch:
- Primary: Hosted Redwood API (region-aware) -> low-latency sites.
- Secondary: Dedicated private pool (for sensitive customers) with model variant pinned.
- Edge fallback: local offline model that periodically pulls curated model delta when connected. On disconnect, local policy uses cached asset descriptors and a strict output filter.
- Fallback severity levels: informational -> allow lower-quality small model; critical safety recommendations -> block on local model, escalate to human otherwise.

Payload/cost optimization notes:
- Use prefix caching for repeated asset metadata.
- Trim telemetry to 90th percentile of signal features (preprocessor rule).
- Suggest batching low-priority alerts (5s window) at host side to reduce per-token overhead.

Open questions (to resolve with Fenris):
- Which specific asset descriptors are "sacrosanct" (must not leave site)? Get list.
- SLA for offline inference availability? They mentioned 72h offline but want 99.9% when connected — clarify.
- Who owns the local model update cycle (Fenris ops vs RW engineer-managed)?
- Acceptable level of model compression/quantization given quality bar for safety recommendations.

Action items / next steps:
- [Ravi] Send short POC plan w/ two tracks: hosted pilot (4 weeks) + edge trial (6–8 weeks). Due 2025-11-07.
- [Elena] Run quick bench: 7B q4 and 13B float on T4 profile with typical Fenris message payload. Deliver perf numbers by 2025-11-10.
- [Marcus] Share list of site categories (air-gapped / constrained / cloud-connected) and asset descriptor whitelist by 2025-11-06.
- [Priya] Provide 10 red-team prompt examples and 20 historical alert threads for evals by 2025-11-12.
- [Tom] Confirm KMS/HSM options and compliance checklist items; meeting scheduled 2025-11-05.

Notes-to-self (ideas / low-cost experiments):
- Prototype a prompt template that replaces tag ids with short asset labels client-side to keep tokens lower.
- Add a small rule-based fallback for safety-critical phrasing (if model suggests direct control action, require manual confirmation).
- Explore using small distilled policy model on edge to re-rank/validate outputs from hosted model before presenting to tech.

Risks/mitigations:
- Risk: hallucination causing incorrect safety advice. Mitigation: strict filters + require manual confirmation for actuation instructions; conservative language model with uncertainty tokens.
- Risk: model updates breaking behavior. Mitigation: pin model versions for production routes, use canary rollout + replay evals.

Quick timeline sketch for POC:
- Week 1: requirements, data sample exchange, benching (host+edge).
- Week 2–5: hosted POC + fast feedback loop with Fenris ops.
- Week 6–12: deploy local edge on 2 test substations (one cloud-connected, one air-gapped) and measure behavior under disconnect.

Random scribbles:
- Consider small vocabulary mapping file shipped as part of local agent (json list of id->label).
- Could leverage Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching config once we have token distribution.

End ramble. Keep this as working doc — will convert to a short one-pager after we get sample telemetry and perf numbers.
